text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed lower across the board in quiet dealings. Turnover was light dominated by trades in the two nearby positions. August lost $1.90 to close at $313 per tonne, while October closed $1.30 lower at $305 per tonne. Raw sugar futures in New York closed lower across the board although prices remained within their recent trading range. The trade continued to roll short May positions into July, pushing the nearby spread as wide as 0.47 at one point, before it settled at 0.42. Players are expected to begin to address the heavy speculative long position in July once the spot month expires, traders said.

The commitment of traders report, released after the close Friday, showed the speculators to be holding about 66,500 longs as of last Tuesday's close. May lost 6 points to close at 11.49 cents/lb, while July gave up 7 points to close at 11.07 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 3 and 6 points. There was no fresh news to influence prices. London trade house E.D.& F. Man said in its latest monthly sugar report that the upside potential for world sugar prices is still limited despite a reduction in the overall statistical surplus.

Man said raw sugar values could be pressured after the nearby May expiry as new southern hemisphere supplies from the Center-South Brazil, Australia and South Africa combined with delayed Thai shipments will boost availability. But Russian raws demand could also pick up with the recent imposition of a tax on white sugar, it said. In white sugar Man said current dry weather concerns would support prices although in the longer term much would depend on the progress of EU crops. Even though it has been very dry and cold in many beet growing areas this month, it is far too early in the season to make any firm predictions. Moreover, the sugar beet has enormous recuperative powers so that the outcome is still open.

EUROPEAN UNION - The area sown to sugar beet in the European Union (EU) should total 2.05 million ha in 1997/98, just 1.2 percent up on 2.03 million ha in 1996/97, trade house E.D.& F. Man said. This is exactly in line with our estimate released on March 13. Man said the higher yields in 1996/97 had prompted farmers in some member states to decrease their sowing areas marginally.

NORWAY - Sugar imports in March 1997 amounted to 13,172 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 15,329 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first quarter of 1997 (January/March) up to 37,617 tonnes against 40,992 tonnes in January/March 1996. Total imports in 1996 amounted to 188,832 tonnes compared to 173,712 tonnes in 1995. Major countries of origin in January/March 1997 were Denmark with 17,504 tonnes whites against 25,872 tonnes, the United Kingdom with 9,233 tonnes against 9,656 tonnes and Sweden with 5,188 tonnes against 21 tonnes.

CUBA - According to ISO figures, sugar exports in January 1997 amounted to 272,904 tonnes, raw value, slightly down on the 277,310 tonnes exported in January 1996. This brought cumulative exports in the first four months of 1996/97 up to 287,531 tonnes against 277,348 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 3.816 million tonnes against 2.760 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in October/January 1996/97 were Iran with 65,061 tonnes raws against nil, Russia with 60,850 tonnes, down from 134,087 tonnes and China with 31,717 tonnes against nil.

The largest countries of destination in calendar year 1996 were Russia with 1.825 million tonnes raws against 722,051 tonnes, China with 432,417 tonnes, down from 683,176 tonnes, Morocco with 206,866 tonnes compared to 88,054 tonnes and Romania with 200,207 tonnes against 95,930 tonnes.
